title: Capacity Sherpa: SLO-driven right-sizing & autoscale plan generator for dedicated fleets
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem: Customers with Dedicated capacity struggle to pick and maintain optimal pool sizes and autoscale settings. They either overprovision (wasted cost) or underprovision (tail latency / dropped requests). Existing advisors are focused on utilization snapshots or batch-level suggestions; we need an SLO-first, action-oriented tool that produces a validated migration plan and autoscale policy tuned to real request shapes.

Goal: Build a "Capacity Sherpa" feature that: (1) ingests per-route/token telemetry and SLO definitions, (2) produces a suggested fleet layout (node counts by GPU type & region), headroom targets, and autoscale policies (scale unit, cooldowns, burst behavior), and (3) validates recommendations with synthetic load replays and cost delta estimates. Output is a one-click plan customers or SREs can apply to Dedicated pools.

Success metrics: recommended pool reduces 95th-percentile cost-per-successful-token by >=10% vs current config without increasing p99 latency by >5%. Recommendations have a clear validation run (synthetic replay) with pass/fail. Uptake: 20% of dedicated customers on trial apply suggestions within first month.

Approach / Implementation sketch:
- Data model: roll up per-route timeseries for RPS, tokens/req, p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency, error-rate, and cache-hit fraction. Use existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> metrics-db) with a short-term high-res window (1s-10s) and longer-term 1m aggregates.
- SLO-driven sizing: convert SLOs (e.g., p99 < 250ms, availability > 99.9) into required tail-serving capacity by using observed tail-latency/throughput curves per model variant and GPU family. Produce conservative and optimistic profiles.
- Synthetic validation: replayer that issues recorded traces at scale to a staging pool with the recommended config; measure latency, KV cache behavior, and token cost. Flag regressions.
- Autoscale policy generator: suggested rules include target utilization bands (e.g., keep token-serializer queue latency < X ms), minimum/maximum nodes, scale step (granularity), cooldowns, and fallback model variants when scale cannot catch up. Include cost ceiling guard rails.
- UI/Output: single JSON plan with human-readable summary, delta estimates (cost/month), expected latency impact, validation run link, and a one-click apply (subject to customer approval).

Trade-offs & open questions:
- Accuracy of tail-latency extrapolation: models for p99.9 vs throughput may be noisy for low-volume routes. Proposal: require a minimum historical volume threshold and fall back to conservative default multipliers when volume is low.
- Synthetic replay fidelity vs production side effects: replay may not perfectly reproduce cold-cache or multi-tenant interference. We'll include cache warm-up and two-phase validation (warmup + full-run) and annotate confidence bands.
- Granularity of recommendations: per-pool vs per-route. Start with per-pool recommendations with optional per-route suggestions for high-impact routes.

Data sources & artifacts:
- Existing dashboards: Grafana - /d/dedicated/fleet-utilization (internal)
- Example SLO definitions: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/slo-playbook
- Prototype replay service PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-service/pull/142

Deliverables:
- Backend service to compute recommendations and run validations (team-owned microservice).
- Frontend flow in Console: "Capacity Sherpa" card inside Dedicated pool settings with plan preview and validation results.
- Telemetry and audit logs for applied plans, including rollback API.

Notes for reviewers: prioritize correctness of SLO-to-capacity transform and safety of the one-click apply. We must not auto-terminate nodes without an explicit approval flow.
acceptance_criteria: System ingests per-route telemetry and can produce a recommended pool size and autoscale JSON plan for any Dedicated pool with >= 3 days of history.
Synthetic validation run executes against a staging pool and reports p50/p95/p99/p99.9 latency, error-rate, and token cost; pass/fail decision computed automatically.
Console shows plan summary, cost delta, and a guarded one-click apply that requires a two-step confirmation and audit log entry.
Applied plans include rollback metadata and do not exceed customer-configured cost ceiling or min/max node constraints.

suggested_implementation_steps: Build telemetry adapter: aggregate per-route token/time series and store pre-computed throughput-latency curves.
Implement SLO-to-capacity transformer with conservative/optimistic profiles and volume-threshold gating.
Wire replay-service to run validations against staging pools with cache warmup and full-run phases.
Implement autoscale policy generator: output format compatible with existing Dedicated autoscaler and include safety checks.
Create Console UX: plan preview, confidence score, validation run report, and guarded one-click apply with audit log.
Run internal dogfood across 3 pilot customers and iterate based on regressions or false positives.
